samples: This program fetches the current weather for Berlin from the Open-Meteo API, parses the JSON response into typed weather data, and prints the temperature and wind speed to the console. If the HTTP request or JSON parsing fails, it converts those failures into a weather-specific error. It is useful if you want a small command-line weather display, but it depends on network access and only reports one location.

If the HTTP request fails or the response is not valid JSON, it converts those failures into a weather-specific error. It is useful if you want a small command-line weather display, but it depends on network access and only reports one location.

This program fetches the current weather for Berlin from the Open-Meteo API, then prints the temperature and wind speed to the console. It includes a reusable network function for downloading and parsing the forecast JSON, and a small error type to distinguish unreachable API failures from malformed responses. Use it if you want a simple example of calling an HTTP API and displaying live weather data, but note that it depends on network access to Open-Meteo and console output.
